text:
ben_acme: Hey team — our customers are seeing streamed responses from the /v1/stream endpoint stop mid-event. They get a few SSE lines and then the connection dies. Client reconnects a bunch and they see duplicate partial outputs. Repro steps below, happening only when Cloudflare proxy is enabled.

ben_acme: Repro: curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.acme.example.com/v1/stream?session=abc123
Received: data: {"chunk":"hello"}

...then nothing, connection closed after ~18s. No final event, no ERROR.

ben_acme: We tried bypassing Cloudflare (pointing DNS to ALB) and the stream stays healthy. So this looks like edge buffering or idle timeout with Cloudflare+ALB. Customer upset — want urgent guidance.

alice_support: thanks for the details, ben. can you paste any edge headers you see in the truncated responses? specifically CF-Cache-Status, via, x-amzn-trace-id, or any proxy-related headers?

ben_acme: headers I can share:
Server: envoy
CF-Cache-Status: DYNAMIC
Via: 1.1 vegur
X-Amzn-Trace-Id: Root=1-00000000-000000000000000000000000
content-encoding: gzip
transfer-encoding: chunked

ben_acme: Also saw an upstream log line: "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream" right around disconnect time.

maya_sre: this rings a bell — Cloudflare will sometimes buffer a response when it thinks compression will yield more efficient transfer, especially when it terminates HTTP/2 from client and talks HTTP/1.1 to backend. If the edge buffers compressed chunks, you can get partial visible output + abrupt close when buffer is flushed/closed.

maya_sre: couple quick checks: 1) can you reproduce when forcing "Accept-Encoding: identity" (i.e., disable gzip) in curl? 2) can you add small periodic heartbeats from the server (

) every 10s to avoid idle close?

ben_acme: forcing identity did make the behaviour better — stream stayed open longer and messages arrived as expected. So gzip seems involved.

omar_infra: pinging infra. we saw earlier issues where responses compressed at edge caused the proxy to buffer until end-of-stream because there was no Content-Length. Cloudflare/ALB combo + envoy/nginx can do that. The quick customer-facing workarounds:
- disable Cloudflare proxy (set DNS to bypass)
- set content-encoding: identity on server side for SSE endpoints
- ensure SSE sends frequent frames (

) so the edge can't compress into a single large chunk

omar_infra: longer term we should: check our nginx/envoy config for "proxy_buffering on/off" and ensure streaming routes have buffer disabled and X-Accel-Buffering: no header set. Also ALB idle timeout default is 60s — consider raising to 120s for long-lived streams.

alice_support: for the customer i propose: 1) temporary patch to set Accept-Encoding: identity on requests from their clients (if they control client) or 2) we can add a response header to opt-out of compression for streaming endpoints. We can roll the header via edge config.

ben_acme: option 2 would be preferred. can you add a header from our service side? we don't control Cloudflare to toggle at their edge.

maya_sre: we can push a small rule in the proxy layer to add "Content-Encoding: identity" or strip "Content-Encoding: gzip" for /v1/stream. I'll open an infra change but need approval for a minor deploy.

sara_prod: tagging product — we should also add an internal doc about SSE + edge compression pitfalls and recommend adding server-side heartbeats. audience: customers using streaming APIs behind proxies.

ben_acme: extra datapoint — client experiences a reconnect storm: since the connection dies mid-event the client retries immediately and our backend sees spikes of repeated partial prompts. Leads to duplicate charges/units. Any rate-limit suggestions?

maya_sre: agree — add jitter and exponential backoff on reconnect to reduce thundering herd. Also, in the short term we can set a server-side idempotency flag — if session sees duplicate token from reconnect, suppress duplicate billing for the overlapping window. Ops can help scope.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: infra/disable-stream-compression v1 -> staging. Change request ID: CR-5943. ETA 12m.

omar_infra: status update: I opened INFRA-2972 to audit streaming routes. Proposed quick fix: add header "X-Accel-Buffering: no" and ensure nginx config for streaming vhosts has 
proxy_buffering off; proxy_max_temp_file_size 0; chunked_transfer_encoding on;
This has fixed similar cases where gzip + chunked produced buffering.

maya_sre: we should also validate Cloudflare feature flags — there is a response buffering setting that may be enforced for some plans. If customer is on proxied mode and enterprise features, edge may still buffer/optimize. When possible recommend customers to use 'DNS only' for critical streaming endpoints or use a subdomain that bypasses proxy.

ben_acme: thanks — client can switch DNS soon, but they'd prefer us to flip header. any ETA on that deploy?

deploy-bot: Deployment INFRA change CR-5943 -> started. Staging passed. Prod rollout in 8 minutes.

alice_support: following up: we rolled header strip + X-Accel-Buffering on /v1/stream at 1979999290. Ben, can you retest now?

ben_acme: retested — stream looks stable with Cloudflare proxy on. No mid-event truncation in 10+ runs. reconnect storms stopped. Will monitor for a day and report back.

maya_sre: great. next actions:
- infra to keep INFRA-2972 open and add tests for streaming endpoints behind proxies
- product to add note to docs and add warning in console when creating streaming keys behind proxied domains
- support to advise customers to prefer heartbeat messages and idempotency windows

ben_acme: appreciated. please send a short postmortem/email to my SRE team summarizing steps taken so we can close the ticket.

omar_infra: will do — adding config diffs and a short root-cause blurb to the ticket. Root cause summary: edge compression + HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation caused buffering at Cloudflare/edge; missing streaming opt-outs (no X-Accel-Buffering, gzip on) caused partial buffering and abrupt connection close when buffers flushed, leading to client reconnect loops.

alice_support: closing loop for now. reopen if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
